--- Page 1 (Beckerman_94a) --- Dear Parents Ruth: Have been waiting to hear from you all much but so far have received nothing but a letter from Abe. So far things are going great. I've really been having a grand time and keeping myself quite busy at it. By the way it's eleven o'clock and I'm listening to Bob Hope's program — and must be 10 o'clock in N.Y.C. Have visited San Francisco (about 40 miles from here) Sat Sunday a Monday. It's the closest thing to N.Y.S. so far... Large city, crowded streets, people etc. The weather here continues to be very peculiar: it's warm during the day, dryish. The early part of the night is very cold. The men and Bugleman they — I'm ready! you I really love it here. The men with me here are a bunch of wonderful fellows. The raining season soon starts anyway. Tell me. It usually rains from Dec. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_94b) --- To February. Received my pay today but didn't get a chance to go down to the bank yet to take my check. We haven't started training yet for that new office yet, although we're going to get my... Tomorrow's Dec 1st so I guess that [illegible] Transfer I wrote you about in my last letter won't come through. Meanwhile I've been given a new job which I really enjoy immensely. I've been assigned to do temporary duty with a training company. We diet, go on hikes, shoot guns etc. The same thing as we have at camp only instead of taking it I'm giving it. I enjoy it very much since it gives me a chance to be out in the wild and see some of the new places. Now I'm just waiting to hear from you. I've and regards to all of you Jack.
